script: The first artificial satellite was a metal ball about 58 centimeters wide. The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on October 4, 1957. It circled Earth about every 96 minutes. Its radio sent out a simple beeping signal that radio operators around the world could hear. Its batteries ran out after about three weeks. It burned up in the atmosphere in January 1958.
